entrada.titulo: Enhancing anomaly detection and prevention in Internet of Things (IoT) using deep neural networks and blockchain based cyber security

perfil_anterior.problema: IoT devices’ exponential development has raised serious security issues as they are distributed, have limited processing capabilities, and are prone to cyberattacks.
perfil_anterior.limites: Future research will focus on developing lightweight DNN architectures for IoT devices with limited resources

entrada.texto:

(CNNs) for AD research is an interesting conclusion. The author believes some security issues, such as data

practices in depth but highlights problem areas that need further investigation, such as more transparent AI 
systems and improved data integration. The results should accelerate future study and development of DL-based 
AD identification techniques.
Zahra Amiri et al. 38 presented autonomous learning techniques for complex pattern recognition in 
interconnected information systems. Identifying cybersecurity risks, detecting financial fraud, diagnosing 
and monitoring healthcare, biometric identification, tailored marketing, and improving the supply chain 
in interconnected systems are the six areas into which we propose a new categorization system. A thorough 
examination of fundamental aspects such as advantages and disadvantages, modeling environment, and datasets 
reveals the most recent advancements in this field. According to the statistics, Elsevier (26.5%) and Springer 
(11.8%) publish many high-quality publications. The analysis reveals that the most critical elements are accuracy 
(12.9%), mobility (11%), and privacy (8%).
Arash Heidari and Mohammad Ali Jabraeil Jamali 39 introduced IoT intrusion detection systems. IDS aims 
to monitor and analyze network traffic from many sources to identify malicious actions. It is an important 
component of cybersecurity systems. An intrusion detection system (IDS) is a procedure that employs many ways 
to identify harmful actions perpetrated against targets. In addition, a thorough empirical study of IDS methods 
is conducted using the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, which entails categorizing, reviewing, and 
incorporating data from all comparable research that addresses one or more IDS research themes. In addition, 
the author categorizes IDS methods in the IoT as signature-based, anomaly-based, specification-based, or 
hybrid, based on the detection strategy. The authors provide a parametric comparison of the IDS techniques.
Arash Heidari et al.40 offered the Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) routing system for V ANETs 
using Colored Timed Petri Nets (CTPNs). This new modeling approach enables us to assess success across 
many hierarchy levels, with nine pages of thorough analysis utilizing it. This research demonstrates the efficacy 
of the AODV routing system in V ANETs and lays a solid groundwork for its development and testing. It will be 
fascinating to see the comparison between the CTPN-based model and the simulations. In particular, testing 
reveals that the model takes 56 s to discover routes, although it only takes 32 s on average. Furthermore, the 
exercise results agree with the total number of packets the model sends and receives. Not only that, the proposed 
strategy demonstrates a return of 41%. Strict T-tests confirm the reliability of the modeling findings.
Abdullah Ayub Khan et al. 41 suggested the blockchain distributed ledger technology with the Internet 
of Medical Things(BDLT-IoMT) for secure data processing. The innovative, interoperable approach in the 
proposed design addresses the primary issues of secure infrastructure, peer-to-peer communication across 
nodes, and seamless data integrity. Simulation findings show large differences of 1.37%, 1.56%, and 1.87%, 
respectively, demonstrating the approach’s uniqueness. (i) Ensuring the safety of automated decision-making 
via infrastructure security; (ii) Maintaining the integrity of data sharing and exchange; and (iii) Optimizing 
network resources to facilitate communication across diverse devices. These three areas provide the basis for the 
assessment.
Abdullah Ayub Khan et al. 42 proposed the blockchain and augmented intelligence of things for small-
medium enterprise management systems (BAIoT-EMS). The platform’s consortium network and InterPlanetary 
File Storage (IPFS) provide secure storage and transaction management. Smart contracts are used to automate 
and protect activities such as device registration. A unique multi-proof-of-work consensus approach minimizes 
resource usage while analyzing, validating, and verifying AIoT transactions. The simulation results show that the 
suggested framework is successful, with a performance gain of 63.51% and a decrease of 11.75% in computational 
power utilization.
Abdullah Ayub Khan et al. 43 recommended the Blockchain-enabled infrastructural security solution for 
serverless consortium fog and edge computing. The primary goal of this piece is to organize newly published 
research and surveys on the state of the art in edge distributed computing and compute outsourcing, including 
fog and edge. The author presented a distributed outsourced compute architecture that is serverless and built 
on the Hyperledger Sawtooth blockchain. Outsourcing computational ledgers is securely stored in immutable 
storage using this system based on theoretical architecture, which ensures strong data security regarding 
transparency, integrity, provenance, and privacy protection. Differences between the present system and the 
suggested taxonomy according to several criteria, such as privacy and system security, are also highlighted in 
this article.
Abdullah Ayub Khan et al. 44 presented AI, IoT, and Blockchain for future vehicular development. 
Combining AI with the IoT may address Analytics, management, and real-time monitoring issues, such as 
ledger administration and node-to-node data exchange. Flying automobiles are only one example of how this 
article delves into the possible consequences of merging these technologies. Reviewing existing literature on 
intelligent transportation system frameworks, architectures, and methodologies, it pinpoints areas needing 
further study and presents novel, secure sensing processes for application in future transportation systems 
within a user-centric framework. Finally, the article identifies prospective study topics and provides solutions to 
current challenges, highlighting the need to solve implementation concerns and prioritize privacy protection as 
transportation technology grows.

resposta.resumo: O trecho discute a predominância de Python e CNNs em pesquisas de detecção de anomalias (AD) baseadas em DL, apontando lacunas em proteção de dados e estabilidade de modelos. Destaca a necessidade de IA mais transparente e melhor integração de dados. Apresenta diversas propostas de blockchain aplicadas ao IoT, como BDLT‑IoMT para segurança de dados e BAIoT‑EMS para gestão de PMEs, ressaltando ganhos de desempenho e redução de consumo computacional.

resposta.interpretacao: O texto evidencia que, embora haja avanços no uso de DL e blockchain para detecção de anomalias em IoT, ainda faltam abordagens que garantam a proteção de dados e a estabilidade dos modelos, além de necessidade de maior transparência e integração de dados. As propostas de blockchain em diferentes domínios (IoMT, PMEs, fog/edge) sugerem um movimento rumo a soluções mais interoperáveis e eficientes.
